The first day is the same for every case of AR4DS. Its morning sets out why the credibility of social science became a question, the three kinds of repetition that go under the word 'replication', the programme of studies that measured them, and the archives in which open research keeps its materials. Its afternoon teaches the tools of the course live: R, the IDE and Quarto, on the data of the housing-audit case, which the modules use as their running example. Each session is taught from its own deck on the AR4DS site and has a module as its reading, before or after the session.

## 1. Credibility and the three Rs

What a claim in social science is for, false positives and forking paths, the evidence from replications and many-analysts studies, incentives and questionable research practices, and the red-card study, in which twenty-nine teams analysed one dataset. The session then sets out the three Rs, reproduction, robustness and replication, as a matrix of data against analysis, and ends on the practices of open research.

[Open the slides](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/slides/credibility.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Read the glossary](../../resources.qmd#glossary){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

## 2. SCORE and Multi100

The programme and its three studies, of reproducibility, robustness and replicability, how Multi100 chose its claims and set its two tasks, how the results of its analysts were put on a common scale, and what the four cases of the course recorded.

[Open the slides](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/slides/score-multi100.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Read SCORE and Multi100](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/score-multi100.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"} [Read the Multi100 article](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/multi100-article.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

## 3. Repositories and data sources

The three routes by which data reach a researcher, the archives, surveys and statistics of social science with the access rule of each, and the routes of this case from the GESIS archive, the World Bank, Eurostat and the OSF. Then what a repository has to do, the repositories that researchers use, registrations and preregistration templates, and the public record of the case.

[Open the slides](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/slides/repositories.html){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Read Social science data sources](../../companion/data-sources.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"} [Read Reproducibility repositories](../../companion/repositories.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

## 4. R

R taught live: objects and data frames, packages, reading a file and looking at it, the pipe and the datawizard verbs, a share and a difference in shares, a first table and a first figure.

## 5. Positron

The IDE taught live in the workspace: opening the folder, the panes of the window, running code from the editor, the console and the Variables pane, the Data Explorer, plots and help, and the terminal. Participants who work in RStudio or VS Code follow in their own IDE.

## 6. Quarto

The report of the workspace taken apart: what a `.qmd` file holds and what rendering does to it, the header, chunks and their options, inline code, captions and cross-references, citations, and a render from a clean session.
